module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 868

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/868](https://www.erdosproblems.com/868)
- [LaLa26] Larsen and Larsen, [Erdős problem 868](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-868/blob/main/868.pdf) (2026)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos868

/-- The number of ways in which a natural `n` can be written as the sum of
`o` members of the set `A`. Representations are counted as nondecreasing tuples, so that
two representations differing only in the order of their summands are counted once. -/
noncomputable
def ncard_add_repr (A : Set ℕ) (o : ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  { a : Fin o → ℕ | Monotone a ∧ Set.range a ⊆ A ∧ ∑ i, a i = n }.ncard

/-- Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of ways in which
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, then
must $A$ contain a minimal additive basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] answered this in the negative.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_868.parts.i :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      atTop.Tendsto (fun n => ncard_add_repr A 2 n) atTop → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 := by
  sorry

/-- Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of ways in which
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) > \epsilon \log n$ for large $n$
and an arbitrary fixed $\epsilon > 0$, then must $A$ contain a minimal additive
basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] constructed a counterexample with $f(n) > c \log n$ for all large $n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_868.parts.ii :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ᵉ (A : Set ℕ) (ε > 0), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ε * Real.log n < ncard_add_repr A 2 n) → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős and Nathanson proved that this is true if $f(n) > c \log n$ for all large $n$, for
some fixed constant $c > (\log \frac{4}{3})^{-1}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_868.variants.fixed_ε :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ᵉ (A : Set ℕ) (c > (Real.log (4 / 3))⁻¹), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, c * Real.log n < ncard_add_repr A 2 n) → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 := by
  sorry

/-- Härtter and Nathanson proved that there exist additive bases which do not contain
any minimal additive bases. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/hjyuh/formal-conjectures/blob/e0da6ec78953b17618895a093d4bee90fd3f6f67/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/868.lean#L132"]
theorem erdos_868.variants.Hartter_Nathanson (o : ℕ) (ho : 1 < o) : ∃ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o ∧ ∀ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o →
    ∃ b ∈ B, (B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o := by
  sorry

end Erdos868

reformulations.difference: "A contains a minimal additive basis of order 2" is written as `∃ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2`. That is, deleting any single element destroys the basis property. The source (Larsen–Larsen) defines minimal as "contains no proper additive subbasis". parts.ii, variants.fixed_ε and variants.Hartter_Nathanson (order o) use the same encoding.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The basis property is upward closed: if C ⊆ D then o•C ⊆ o•D (`Set.nsmul_subset_nsmul_left`). Suppose some proper subset C ⊊ B were a basis. Pick b ∈ B \ C; then C ⊆ B \ {b}, so B \ {b} is a basis. Conversely, each B \ {b} with b ∈ B is itself a proper subset. I proved `(∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o) ↔ (∀ C ⊂ B, ¬ C.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o)` for every o in /workspace/review/scratch3.lean.

reformulations.difference: f(n), "the number of ways n can be written as the sum of two elements of A", is encoded as the ncard of the set of monotone `a : Fin 2 → ℕ` with range in A and a 0 + a 1 = n. That counts unordered representations, including a = b, rather than ordered pairs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I proved `ncard_add_repr A 2 n = {x : ℕ | x ∈ A ∧ n - x ∈ A ∧ 2 * x ≤ n}.ncard` in /workspace/review/scratch2.lean. This is Larsen–Larsen's r_A(m) = #{(a,b) ∈ A² : a + b = m, a ≤ b}, and it is the convention under which they quote the Erdős–Nathanson constant (log 4/3)^{-1}. For parts.i (f → ∞) and parts.ii (∀ ε > 0), ordered versus unordered counting makes no difference, because r_u ≤ r_o ≤ 2 r_u: 'f → ∞' and '∃ ε > 0, f > ε log n eventually' are the same class of sets A under either count.

reformulations.difference: A ranges over `Set ℕ`, which includes 0. The source (Larsen–Larsen, following Erdős–Nathanson) works with sets of positive integers. The same holds in parts.i and variants.fixed_ε.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Positive-integer sets are a special case, so the Lean universal statement implies the source's. Conversely, take A with 0 ∈ A and put A' = A \ {0}. Then f_{A'}(n) ≥ f_A(n) − 1, since only the pair (0, n) is lost. So A' is still a basis, and still satisfies f → ∞, or f > (ε/2) log n eventually, or f > c' log n eventually for some c' with (log 4/3)^{-1} < c' < c. The source's statement applied to A' gives a minimal basis B ⊆ A' ⊆ A. So each universal statement is equivalent in the two universes, and so is the existence of counterexamples behind the two `answer(False)` claims.

review.notes:
No findings. What was checked:

(1) Lean experiments, all compiling, in /workspace/review:
- scratch2.lean: `ncard_add_repr A 2 n` equals the unordered count r_A(n), and `(Real.log (4/3))⁻¹ > 3`. So `4 / 3` is real division, not ℕ division; ℕ division would make the threshold 0⁻¹ = 0 and collapse fixed_ε into parts.ii.
- scratch3.lean: deleting one element destroys the basis property ⇔ no proper subset is a basis.
- scratch_hn.lean: the fork proof cited by the `formal_proof` attribute on `Hartter_Nathanson` compiles against the current definitions, using only standard axioms. It proves the identical statement with A = {1} ∪ {n | o ∣ n}.
- Also confirmed: `2 • A` elaborates to `Set.NSMul`, the 2-fold sumset.

(2) parts.i and parts.ii with `answer(False)`. Larsen–Larsen, Theorem 1: there exist ε > 0 and A ⊂ ℕ⁺ with r_A(m) > ε log m for all large m, such that A contains no minimal subbasis. They show every subbasis D stays a basis after deleting any one element. This negates both universal statements (f → ∞ follows). The polarity is right and 'research solved' matches the source.

(3) Reading of parts.ii. The Lean takes "f(n) > ε log n for large n and an arbitrary fixed ε > 0" with ∀ ε outside the implication. The other reading, f(n)/log n → ∞, is already settled positively by Erdős–Nathanson, so it cannot be the question. Larsen–Larsen frame it the Lean's way: "They conjectured that this is not true for all positive c. We prove this conjecture."

(4) variants.fixed_ε. Larsen–Larsen state the theorem as: if c > (log 4/3)^{-1} and r_A(m) > c log m for all large m (r_A unordered, a ≤ b), then A contains a minimal subbasis. The Lean matches this exactly. I could not read the site's own wording. If it quotes the bound with the exact constant, or via the ordered count 1_A∗1_A, the Lean would be implied by, not identical to, that wording. It would still match the theorem as its solvers report it.

(5) variants.Hartter_Nathanson. It generalises to every order o ≥ 2. It is true (formally verified), and the o = 2 case is the cited remark. I could not access Härtter 1956 or Nathanson 1974 to confirm they treat general order. Linking a fork with kind `formal_conjectures` is common practice in this repository, so it is not a defect.

(6) Trivia, not reported: the module docstring gives the [LaLa26] title as 'Erdős problem 868', the repository name. The paper's title is 'Robust additive bases without minimal subbases'. The hypothesis `A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2` is redundant in parts.i, parts.ii and fixed_ε, and harmless.

(7) Access limits: the verbatim erdosproblems.com/868 page could not be fetched. Faithfulness was settled against the Larsen–Larsen paper, which restates the problem and the history. The teorth database and a third-party restatement are consistent with the docstrings.
